observation_window.sampling: provider default; not continuous motion capture

extraction.teacher_style: The teachers use a clear, step-by-step approach, explaining the mechanics of each movement. They demonstrate the steps together, providing both male and female perspectives.

lesson_structure.note: Introduction to contra dance and its roots.
Breakdown of the Do-Si-Do and See-Saw.
Breakdown of the Balance and Swing.
Breakdown of the Gypsy and Swing.

metaphors: The Do-Si-Do is like walking in a circle around your partner.
The Allemande is like holding right hands up to each other.
The Balance is a nice filler move.
common_mistakes: Clashing with your partner during a Do-Si-Do.
Uncomfortable about going backwards while facing away from your partner.
safety: If you are not sure where your partner is, just take a peek behind you, make sure you are not colliding with her.

steps_taught.name: Do-Si-Do
steps_taught.description: Walking in a circle around your partner while facing the same direction.

steps_taught.name: See-Saw
steps_taught.description: Do-Si-Do performed in the opposite direction.

steps_taught.name: Allemande
steps_taught.description: Holding hands with your partner and walking around one full time.

steps_taught.name: Balance
steps_taught.description: Taking a step forward and then a step back into place.

steps_taught.name: Swing
steps_taught.description: A dance move where partners hold each other and rotate.

steps_taught.name: Gypsy
steps_taught.description: Staring into each other's eyes while walking around each other in a circle.

steps_taught.name: Promenade
steps_taught.description: Walking together while facing the same direction.

what_hinders: Lack of counting or musical context.

quotes.text: The Do-Si-Do, which involves walking in a circle around our partner.
If you feel uncomfortable about going backwards while facing away from your partner, don't worry.
Allemande is, for example, Allemande right.
We can also do a balance, which is a nice filler move.
We'll do what's called a Gypsy, so we'll stare into each other's eyes.
The promenade just means that we are going for a walk.

evidence_segments.observation: The teachers walk in a circle around each other while facing the same direction.
The teachers hold right hands up and walk around each other.
The teachers join hands, take a step forward, and then a step back.
The male teacher puts his right hand on the female teacher's left shoulder blade, and she puts her left hand on his shoulder.
The teachers walk around each other while maintaining eye contact.
The teachers join left hands, and the female teacher puts her right hand on her shoulder, while the male teacher puts his hand on hers.

extraction.distinctive_method: The teachers use a 'couple' terminology to explain the dance structure, which is helpful for understanding the roles and movements in a group setting.
